Naive Tetrahedral Surfacing is an isosurface extraction method that processes each tetrahedron independently to generate a collection of individual, unconnected polygons [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly describes 'Naive Tetrahedral Surfacing' as a method that processes each tetrahedron independently. It details the algorithm's logic: evaluating scalar values at vertices, partitioning them into 'less than iso' and 'more than iso' lists, and iterating through every pair of points from these two lists to calculate intersection vertices. The evidence notes that this pairwise comparison (e.g., 2 less * 2 more = 4 intersections) is computationally inefficient and may generate redundant geometry, implying that the resulting polygons are generated per-tetrahedron without inherent connectivity guarantees between adjacent tetrahedra (unlike standard methods that ensure manifold connectivity). The claim that it generates a collection of individual, unconnected polygons is supported by the description of the algorithm's local, independent processing and the note that 'duplicate vertices are considered acceptable' and ordering logic doesn't guarantee connectivity.
